summary: Steel tower, 60 ft (18.3 m), erected at Palestine Church in 1927 and reported in use by January 1928; no source found on its current state.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erected at Palestine Church, 10 miles north of Fayetteville, per a Forest Lookouts page that cites the 1926-28 state biennial report.
The Forest Worker (January 1928) lists the 60-foot steel tower on Palistine Hill among the towers in use for the first time.

notes_for_editor: Probably the same tower as us-nc-palestine (see its notes); the two records share the county and the Palestine/Palistine name, and the coordinates are about 2 km apart. The page has one photo (8382948_orig.jpg) with no credit or licence shown, so none is listed. Nothing after January 1928 appears in any source found, and no source describes the site today. WebSearch returned a budget-exhausted error for this run and websearch.py was not used to get around it, so only cached and fetched pages were read. The page's embedded map URL carries lat=35.2102 and long=-78.8264 (raw HTML, not in the extracted text), the figures cited in us-nc-palestine's notes.
